title: Argue the other side
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When did you last argue the other side on purpose?

I said: I am going to play devil's advocate, just for the sake of debate. Show me a medium that has had no limits ever in the history of the world. It is all judgment-based: what is right and what is wrong.
A student answered that you will always have some limit, even social ones: if you feel you may be judged for saying something, it limits what you say.
A student said: it is not a yes or no. How do we balance responsibility with freedom?

Another student said: I will agree it is difficult to call it black and white, so let me give a direction instead of a concise answer. We should head toward systems that take the most people's opinions into consideration, not the fewest people deciding for everyone.
I said that being aware and on our toes about these issues is a positive thing.
What is the strongest argument against your own view?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a view you hold strongly.
Write the strongest argument against it.
Write what a person who disagrees would call a fair test.
Write a direction you would aim for if you cannot give a yes or no.
Write what you changed your mind about, if anything.

check.q: What did I say I was playing?
What did a student say instead of a concise answer?
What did a student say about the question?
choices: It is not a yes or no

recap: Argue the other side on purpose. When there is no clean answer, name a direction.
